content:
This looks quite interesting. The latest update to ChatGPT adds a new Mac integration feature: it can handle conversations from the Apple Messages app. This feature supports iMessage, SMS and RCS.

ChatGPT for Mac now includes the Apple Messages plugin

The new Apple Messages plugin lets ChatGPT read and search chat history on Mac, and prepare and send messages. OpenAI says this feature is available across all plans on the ChatGPT macOS desktop app, and supports ChatGPT Work and Codex.

This kind of access raises concerns about privacy and control, so OpenAI emphasises that, by default, sending messages still requires user approval. Users should be careful before granting persistent approval permissions. OpenAI's plugin guidelines spell out the risks, how to revoke access, and a known issue involving a task that disables the approval prompt.

Here's more from the release announcement:

OpenAI also has a dedicated plugin page detailing how the Messages feature works:

For now, the feature is only available on Macs with Apple silicon; Intel machines are not supported.

If you ask ChatGPT to send a message, it pops up a confirmation prompt before sending. You can choose to skip the confirmation step for individual conversations.

Looking for the new feature inside ChatGPT? This link takes you directly to the Messages plugin in ChatGPT for Mac.

Site co-editing, shared conversation snapshots and more

Although the Messages plugin is the headline new feature for Apple users, this update also includes several other improvements. For example, pinned conversations can now sync between the ChatGPT desktop app and iOS, so users can keep important conversations within reach across Mac and iPhone.

ChatGPT now also lets users share read-only snapshots of local Codex conversations. These snapshots don't change as the original conversation is updated.

Links created from personal accounts can be accessed by anyone with the URL, whereas workspace links are limited to members of that workspace. OpenAI says Codex masks known patterns of confidential information, but reminds users to review snapshots because they may still contain sensitive data.

In addition, Site owners can invite active members of the same workspace to co-edit a Site (if collaboration is available). Editors can update content and database data, save versions, and publish changes after the owner makes the first publication. Owners retain control over access, settings, analytics and version restoration.

Some Site owners can also change the URL hosted by ChatGPT without redeploying, and the old address will automatically redirect to the new one.

Finally, the Computer History feature launched last week will be expanded to Pro, Business and Enterprise users in the European Economic Area, Switzerland and the UK. This optional feature requires Memories to be enabled and is off by default.

You can see the full release announcement for this update here.
